thread.title: Morning Movers: Alcoa Soars as Aluminum Prices Skyrocket…and Earnings, Too - Barron's

author: Ben Levisohn
title: Morning Movers: Alcoa Soars as Aluminum Prices Skyrocket…and Earnings, Too - Barron's
text:
By Ben Levisohn April 19, 2018 9:21 a.m. ET Stocks are heading for a lower open this morning as commodity prices rally.
Illustration: Getty Images S&P 500 futures have fallen 0.3%, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures have declined 58 points, or 0.2%. Nasdaq Composite futures have dropped 0.4%.
But it's the commodity complex that should have our attention. Oil has gained 1.3% to $69.34 this morning, while aluminum has climbed 6.4%, and nickel has jumped 8.3%. And those gains are reflected in pre-open trading in exchange-traded funds this morning, as the Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) has advanced 0.3% to $73.80, and don't be surprised if the Materials Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLB) also get s a boost.
Market technicians are getting really excited about the moves. "Commodities [are] nearing the end to Bear Phase," writes the Technical View's Andrew Addison. BofA Merrill Lynch's Paul Ciana, meanwhile, writes that "our base case view of the Thomson Reuters equal weight commodity index (CCI) suggests commodity markets are on the verge of signaling a secular bull trend."
But a word of warning--some commodities could be nearing a pause. That has Ciana noting that the "rally so far led by energy and metals, the rallies in gold and silver are young while oil and copper have room to trend." As for oil, Sundial Capital Research's Jason Goepfert notes that the rally has hit a point where prices rise only 42% of the time over the next month, while averaging a 0.1% decline.
It's a reminder that just because an asset class finally has everyone's attention doesn't mean it's time to buy. — Ben Levisohn
Morning Movers: Earnings & News
Alcoa (AA) is up 3.3% to $61.33 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The steel maker said it earned 77 cents a share on revenue of $3.09 billion, while analysts were looking for earnings of 68 cents a share on revenue of $3.16 billion. Alcoa also raised its full-year earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization forecast, as it now expects to earn between $3.5 billion and $3.7 billion, up from its previous forecast of $2.6 billion to $2.8 billion.
Amazon.com (AMZN) is up 1.4% to $1,548.94 after announcing it has reached more than 100 million Prime subscribers worldwide.
Illustration: Bloomberg News American Express (AXP) is up 3.4% to $98.40 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The card issuer said ti earned $1.86 a share on revenue of $9.72 billion, while analysts were looking for earnings of $1.71 a share on revenue of $9.49 billion. For the full year, it expects to earn between $6.90 and $7.30 a share, compared to the $7.10 per-share consensus. Evercore's David Togut raised his price target on the shares by $10, to $104, but reiterated an In-Line rating, writing that "With heightened provisioning, which could be up an estimated 34% in 2018 combined with a persistent competitive rewards environment in the U.S., and headwinds to both revenue growth and expenses for the remainder of 2018, we believe AXP is fully valued."
Blackstone (BX) is up 2% to $32.40The asset manager said it earned 65 cents a share on revenue of $1.77 billion, while analysts were looking for earnings of 50 cents a share on revenue of $1.25 billion. Assets under management grew 22% year over year to a record $449.6 billion.
Danaher (DHR) is up 1.6% to $104 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The industrial giant said it earned 99 cents a share on revenue of $4.7 billion, while analysts were looking for earnings of 94 cents a share on revenue of $4.54 billion. For the full year, it raised its guidance, as it now expects to earn $4.38 to $4.48 a share, compared to the $4.41 consensus.
Kinder Morgan (KMI) is up 2.4% to $16.55 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The energy firm said it earned 22 cents a share, a penny above consensus, on revenue of $3.42 billion, below the $3.56 billion average analyst estimate. For the full year, it expects to declare dividends of 80 cents a share and achieve discounted cash flow of $4.57 billion, or $2.05 a share.
Pier One Imports (PIR) is down 18.5% to $2.82 after reporting fiscal fourth-quarter earnings . The home furnishings maker said it earned 21 cents a share on revenue of $512.23 million, while analysts were looking for earnings of 19 cents a share on revenue of $537.62 million. Same-store sales were down 7.5% in the quarter.
Philip Morris International (PM) is down 4.7% to $96.70 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The tobacco seller earned $1 a share on revenue of $6.9 billion, while analysts were looking for earnings of 88 cents on revenue of $7.03 billion. For the full year, it sees earnings per share of $5.25 to $5.40, compared to the $5.26 consensus.
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) is down 5.1% to $39.80 after reporting first-quarter earnings. The chipmaker said it earned $3.46 a share on revenue of $248.08 billion, while analysts were looking for earnings of $3.48 a share on revenue of $250.89 billion. For the second quarter, it expects revenues between $7.8 billion and $7.9 billion, citing weak smartphone demand, compared to the $8.79 billion consensus. Apple (AAPL) is also falling on the news, as it's down 1.7% to $174.80.
United Rentals (URI) is down 2.8% to $174.98 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The equipment rental firm said it earned $2.87 a share on revenue of $1.73 billion, while analysts were looking for earnings of $2.50 a share on revenue of $1.68 billion. for the full year, it expects revenues of $7.3 billion to $7.6 billion, compared to the $7.58 billion consensus. It also authorized a new $1.25 share repurchase program.
Wynn Resorts (WYNN) is up 1.1% to $195 after expanding its board of directors. "The creation of a more diversified board will benefit both the company and shareholders in addition to clearing up any lingering issues left behind by former CEO Steve Wynn," says Trip Miller, Managing Partner at Gullane Capital Partners. "Our only drawback with these three appointees is the lack of gaming experience." — Teresa Rivas
Upgrades & Downgrades
Align Technology (ALGN) has dropped 4% to $266 after getting cut to Equal Weight from Overweight at Morgan Stanley.
Illustration: Bloomberg News Clorox (CLX) is down 2.1% it $124.15 after Morgan Stanley downgraded it to Underweight.
iRobot (IRBT) has gained 5.1% to $64.95 after getting upgraded to Overweight from Neutral at Piper Jaffray.
Sprint (S) is up 1.2% to $6.07 after Macquarie upgraded it to Neutral.
Textron (TXT) is up 1% to $64.61 after Bank of America Merrill Lynch double upgraded it to Buy from Underperform.
Walmart (WMT) is up 0.6% to $88.10 after Argus upgraded it to Buy. — T.R.
